content.text: Erase the narrowest ellipse without touching other itmes using Eraser tool in Excalidraw.
I'll help you erase the narrowest ellipse in Excalidraw. Let me first take a screenshot to see the current state of the canvas.
I can see multiple overlapping ellipses. Let me zoom in to better identify the narrowest ellipse - the one with the smallest width (thinnest horizontally).

Now I can clearly see the ellipses. The narrowest ellipse is the very thin, tall vertical one in the center-left area - it looks almost like a thin sliver/leaf shape. This ellipse has the smallest width (narrowest horizontally).

In the original screenshot, this narrow vertical ellipse runs roughly from around (860, 300) at the top to (870, 530) at the bottom, and it's very thin horizontally. Let me identify its exact position more precisely.

Looking at the zoomed image, the narrow vertical ellipse is centered around x=140 in the zoomed view, which corresponds to approximately x=880 in the original. It spans vertically and is very thin.

Let me select the Eraser tool first.

The Eraser tool is now selected. The narrowest ellipse is the thin vertical sliver-shaped ellipse in the center. Its outline is clearly visible - it runs from about (870, 305) at the top down to (865, 530) at the bottom, and it's very thin horizontally.

To erase only this ellipse without touching others, I need to click precisely on a part of its outline that doesn't overlap with other ellipses. The best spot would be on the left or right edge of this thin ellipse where it's isolated. 

Looking carefully, the widest point of this thin ellipse (around y=420) has its left edge around x=858 and right edge around x=890. However, these may overlap other shapes. A safer approach is to click on the top or bottom curve of this narrow ellipse. Let me look at the top portion around (878, 310) where the narrow ellipse's outline is distinct.

Let me click carefully on the outline of the narrow ellipse - I'll target the right edge of the thin ellipse where it curves, around (888, 420).

The narrowest ellipse (the thin vertical sliver-shaped ellipse) has been successfully erased. Comparing the before and after screenshots, the thin vertical ellipse that ran through the center is now gone, while all the other ellipses remain intact.

Let me verify by zooming into the area where the narrow ellipse used to be to confirm it's completely gone and no other elements were affected.

The task has been completed successfully. The narrowest ellipse—the thin, vertical sliver-shaped ellipse that ran through the center of the drawing—has been completely erased using the Eraser tool.

Comparing the zoomed views before and after:
- **Before:** There was a very thin, tall vertical ellipse (almost like a leaf/lens shape) in the center of the composition.
- **After:** That narrow ellipse is now gone, while all the other wider ellipses remain fully intact and untouched.

The narrowest ellipse was removed precisely without affecting any of the surrounding overlapping ellipses.
